newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-ARSENAL, MANCHESTER UNITED REPORTED IN BIG RIVAL BIDS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ARSENAL, MANCHESTER UNITED REPORTED IN BIG RIVAL BIDS.

text.p: Manchester United and Arsenal are ready to mount rival bids for Real Madrid strikers Davor Suker and Predrag Mijatovic in a package that could be worth five billion pesetas ($38.1 million), according to Spanish media reports.

Both Arsenal and United are said to be interested in buying both players with reports suggesting Arsenal officials are travelling to the Spanish capital to watch Real's Cup game with Valladolid on Thursday before meeting the players themselves the following day.

Mijatovic, a Montenegrin who plays for Yugoslavia, and Suker, who made headlines with some inspired displays for Croatia's during Euro 96, have clocked up 22 league goals between them already this season.
Real coach Fabio Capello was philosophical when asked about the alleged bid for his Balkan strike force on Wednesday.
"Everybody wants players from Real, it's normal, and the English now are the clubs that have got most money of all," said Capello.
The Italian also hit out at Serbian midfielder Dejan Petkovic, who he accused of not training hard enough
"For me he doesn't have the quality to be at Real," said Capello in characteristically blunt fashion.
Petkovic could be the player sacrificed from the squad if Real's bid for Monaco striker Thierry Henry comes off.

Meanwhile, arch-rivals Barcelona have denied that another much-heralded transfer had reached fruition. The club has countered reports that terms have been reached with England's Middlesbrough for the transfer of defender Miguel Angel Nadal.
Nadal had already been approached by Manchester United, but is understood to be happier about staying at Barcelona after regaining his first-team place.

The flurry of transfer news ahead of the closing of the Spanish market on January 15 has also increased speculation that Brazilian World Cup striker Bebeto would leave struggling Sevilla for his old club, Deportivo Coruna.

Bebeto pulled up in training on Tuesday, and was set to miss Wednesday's Cup game against Deportivo. By playing in the match, his fifth competitive game for Sevilla, he would have become automatically ineligible to play for another Spanish club this season.
The injury, which followed Bebeto's absence from the squad to play Rayo Vallecano over the weekend because of a cold, has provoked some cynical comments in the Spanish press.
Bebeto denied he was unhappy in Seville, but acknowledged he was worried about his future.
"Sevilla have many economic problems and I have three children, a family," said the striker.
